text: I am Wayne S. Aho. We are gathered here in Kalamazoo, Michigan, at the home of Reverend John Brinson. The date is March 2, 1958.
This recording is made for the purpose of supplying Americans and other peoples that
were familiar with or heard of the original experience of Reinhold Schmidt at Kearney,
in Nebraska on November 5, 1957, and the various events that occurred after he reported sighting
a spaceship at Kearney, Nebraska, at that time.
With my work in Washington, D.C., I began to investigate this situation.
I had a friend at Kearney, Nebraska, look into this situation.
Correspondence went back and forth, and I received certain material and information
indicate that this man was telling of a true experience and that he had been subjected
to very inhuman treatment because of the fact that he reported this experience.
I called the Hastings State Mental Hospital in Nebraska to try to talk with this man in
person after he had been taken to the state mental hospital, I was told by the superintendent
of the institution that he could not come to the telephone, that it was necessary to
protect him from the public and the public from him.
We are going to make brief statements at this time indicating what our attitude or what
information has come to our attention up to this time, and Mr. Reinhold Schmitt, who is
present here and has appeared with me at several cities on a lecturing tour, Davenport, Iowa,
Tipton, Iowa, Toledo, Ohio, and Kalamazoo, Michigan, will make a statement as to his
experience and what has transpired from November 5th on.
Also, we are going from Kalamazoo, Michigan, to Cardinal, Nebraska, for a series of two
lectures for March 5 and 6.
They will be given at the National Guard Armory there, and appearing with us and in support
of the program will be John Otto of Chicago, Illinois.
Now I'll turn this microphone over to Reverend John Brinson.
I am John Brinson, chairman of the Michigan Flying Saucer Federation.
We have just completed a three-day meeting, which it has been our privilege here in Kalamazoo
to have Wayne S. Aho as speaker and Reinhold Smith.

have had the experience, my wife and I, of having Reinhold Smith and Major Wayne
Wayne Aho in our home and I have every reason to believe that

I am Reinald Schmidt from 1715 Gate Street, Bakersfield, California.
I am a grain buyer working for a firm out of Los Angeles.
I was sent to Kearney, Nebraska, the latter part of October.
On November the 5th, 1957, I was out investigating some grain fields.
I drove four miles south, a mile east, inspecting a field of miles there.
I turned off the highway onto a country road to be out of traffic.
After inspecting the field, I drove up a little farther to a farm gate to turn around.
Just before I got to the farm gate, I noticed a flash ahead of me about a quarter of a mile.
I thought maybe there was blasting trees there although I didn't hear no report.
I thought I'd go up and see what it was.
When I got within a hundred feet or so, I sighted what I thought was a balloon head crash there.
I got a little closer. My car stopped within seventy feet of the river bank.
I got out of my car, walked up to the river bank, and approaching around a corner of some
willows and tall grass, I noticed there was no balloon at all.
It was a large silver object sitting there on four, what I took to be a four-hydronic
ram.
I was, by this time I was within 30 feet of the object.
I, just about that time, a light had shot out of the side of the machine toward me.
and I was stopped in my tracks. I couldn't move my arms nor my feet. I couldn't walk.
This very instance the doors had opened. Two men came out of the ship, asked me whether I was
armed. I told them I was not. They said they would have to search me anyway. What they did,
they didn't take anything from me. By this time I could start moving my arms and my legs again.
I asked them what the machine, what kind of machine it was, or what they were doing there.
me that and I asked them whether I could get closer to the machine and see it. They said
yes, as long as we can't leave for a few minutes anyway, you're just welcome in to look around.
We walked into the, we got into the machine from the appearance from the outside of the
machine was completely, there was no portals, no windows, looks like you're just looking
again at a solid aluminum ship of some kind. When you got inside of the machine, it is
All is very transparent. You can look up, see the sky. You can look down, see the grass.
Look through both sides and see the countryside around us.
In this machine were four men and two ladies.
There's one man who was with me at all times.
The other man was working on an instrument panel.
On the farthest end of the ship was a large desk with two ladies operating the instrument.
I asked them several things about the ship, where they came from, and what they were doing
here, and they said they couldn't tell me that at this time.
These men were dressed in street clothes, the same as any of us Americans are here.
In fact, they could be walking along the streets, and unless you had seen them before, you would
never identify them.
They spoke, this one man spoke to me in American language with a German accent.
Amongst themselves, when they got close to where I was standing, I could tell that they were talking in a high German language, a very good high German.
This panel was, well I say the inside of the ship, the entire ship that we found out later on was 100 feet long, 30 feet wide, and I guess it would be 14 feet high.
The inside panel or the room we were in was approximately 50 feet long and 30 feet wide.
There were two compartments on each end that I didn't get in there.
in there. But the ship, the big room where I was in, they had a panel on one side of
the room, approximately 45 feet long and 5 feet high, completely covered with instruments.
After they, I was in the ship for about 30 minutes. After they got it, whatever they

that they were ready for the takeoff.

see whether I could find some address

Whenever they'd want to go from one end of the ship to the other they would just step back about a foot or a half a step and glide from one end to the other.
I got on that same panel, but it wouldn't work with me, so they must have some contact on their shoes or something.
When they got ready to leave, I stepped out of the ship.
The door slid shut, and I heard a large, sounded like a large motor start operating.
Then the faster the momentum speeded up, the quieter it got.
Pretty soon it took right straight up into the air.
within about 150 feet there was a flash of light and it disappeared completely out of sight.
At that time, that certain day, it was hazy and misting,
but the ceiling was at least 1,000 feet, but it disappeared about 150 feet.

Now, in the newspaper accounting, and I think on radio around here at least,
They said something about propellers whirring as the thing took off.
Now you have told us that this was not true.
Would you explain more thoroughly that there was or was not any moving part visible as the thing took off?
There were no parts visible, but in these two compartments that I never got into,
one on each end of the machine, there was a tube approximately 12 feet in diameter running straight up and down.
I could just see the fans where the way it was sitting there on the east end of the machine on
top there looked like about a 10 bladed fan and this is what I thought made the whirring noise
but there were no propellers these plans these fans were laying flat inside the machine and he's
10 12 foot tubes in other words they were more of an exhaust type fan if you think of it and
a ventilator yes I would think so although when it took off there was no breeze around the ship
Thank you.

Yes. They told me...

and they will see it again.
and in the near future they will know what it's all about.
Another question.
When this ship began to take off, did it remain constant in color,
or did you observe a change in color as it raised and downed to?
No, there was three different changes in color.
The first color would have left the ground approximately 15, 20 feet.
It turned to a pitch black.
It got up a little higher, changed colors again to a bluish green.
The last flash was a real bright flash and it disappeared before my eyes.
They uh, after they had taken, just before they started taking off they said to me not
to try to start my car because it wouldn't start anywhere.
This is the first I knew that they had stopped my car.
I got in my car and drove to Kearney, Nebraska.
I didn't know just what to do.
I knew part of the people would believe it and the other half probably wouldn't.
I had seen a lot of advertising at the Air Force, one of the sky watchers,
that we should report any flying objects that we've seen.
I drove to Kearney, Nebraska and looked for the Lutheran minister.
I was going to ask him what to do, what he thought that to do.
He didn't happen to be home that day, so I drove to the police department and asked for the sheriff.
They said he was over at the courthouse.
I went over to the courthouse, told my story to the sheriff, and he said we will go out there and look.
The sheriff and I drove out to this place, and on the way out there, the sheriff told me,
He said this was quite a coincidence.
Just before noon today, he asked whether I heard the siren blow.
I had heard. If I was in a hotel, I thought it was a fire.
But he said someone had reported an unidentified object flying toward Kearney, a strange ship.
But I never heard any more about that.
We drove out to the place where the ship had been setting,
It had been setting, and he definitely said there was outlines of a large machine that had been setting there.
And we also found some oil was on the ground there.
I asked him then whether we should, didn't think we should rope this off
or put guards out there and call Washington or someone that had the official capacity of taking care of a deal like this.
He said, well, we'll go back to Kearney and get some more of the officials and see what they say.
back to the police department we called we told our stories to the chief of police and later on

I wanted more information also at the police department.
They were swamped with calls.
They came over and asked whether I would come over and answer the telephone,
help them answer the telephones there at the police department.
The chief of police turned his office over to me, closed the door.
There were two telephones in there.
I answered these two telephones as fast as I could.
The chief of police was out in the other room answering.
That's right.
And at 9.30 that night the chief of police made an appointment with a local radio station.
He went on the station with me for about an hour's interview over the air.
He verified my story.
Also that same night at 10.30 we went on TV.
He was with me on TV verifying my story.
We still have the original tape recording that was made that night.
Later on we went back to the police department again.
There were a lot of photographers that flew in and the police department completely swamped
with photographers and news people and telephone calls.
This went on for approximately 18 hours.
The Air Force from Colorado Springs flew out.
They asked me the same question I repeated, and they made a tape recording of it,
and they went back to Colorado Springs.
Shortly after that is when everybody wanted to change their story.
The chief of police, the sheriff, the county attorney, and some more told me that they didn't think that this story was true,
that they were going to change their story and wanted me to change it too.
I told them no. I said I came to this ship just the way I had it.
I explained it several different times and it was a true story and I was going to stick with it.
They had several different remarks to make.
They said that they had heard that I smoked marijuana and several different deals like that.
The next morning about 5 o'clock they asked whether I would take a lie detector test.
I had been talking for about 18-20 hours. My voice was getting very hoarse. I had a
headache and I had to have nothing to eat all day. And I said, no, I would not go to
night anymore. But after a few hours rest, I would go to Grand Island, Nebraska and have
a lie detector test. Next morning they came out with a paper that I refused to have a
lie detector test. I did refuse it that night because I couldn't talk anyway and I didn't
think that was the time to go. The next morning I asked them whether they want to go and take
a lie detector test and they said no it wasn't necessary. The following morning at about
10 o'clock they brought an oil can to the jail where I had stayed all night and they
said that I just want to change my story now because they found evidence of some oil. The
The oil had been poured on the ground, and they found a new can of oil lying there where the ship had been sitting.
The night before, the Air Force, myself, all officials, and besides from 500 to 1,000 persons,
had walked up and down that river where this machine had been sitting.
Nobody had found the oil can there that evening.
The next morning after I got live here, they had laid a new oil can right on the plain side where the ship had been sitting.
I had to come up with a different story than that because there sure couldn't have been
that many people blind to see that oil can the night before.
I said if you think I had anything to do with that oil can, I should take some fingerprints
off of it because they didn't do that.
They said they found this oil can in the back of my car.
I told them I had two cans of oil in the back of my car with rice, but it wasn't the kind
of cans that they were showing me.
I had also a can opener in my car that would open a triangular hole.
At least this can was opened with a round can opener.
After I got back to my car again, I've seen where they had poured oil in the back of my car over some of my laundry.
And the two cans of oil that I had in my car were still there.
They started then, they wanted to give me a test for the mental hospital.
I'd seen what they were trying to do, so I just went right along with them.
I didn't fight them after they kept me in jail for three days.
I was admitted to the mental hospital at Hastings, Nebraska.
I stayed there for two weeks.
Before we go farther, I have a few questions that I would like to ask at this time.
When you were on this ship originally, how did you feel about the possibility of getting

Did you think that you were going to ever get off again?
No, I didn't think I'd ever get off that ship.
I was very much pleased and relieved when they told me I should leave.

I did that for Carly Nebraska. I was quite scared that that was all over with.
Now, what about this oil that was on the ground originally?

And where was it sent? It was sent to...the sheriff and I picked it up in a little bottle.

The chief of police, Mattel, got some on our hands when we were picking it up off the roof
there.
and we both mentioned it after we were on TV that we could still smell that oil on our fingers.

Whether it came out of the ship, I wouldn't say because I've never seen where it came out of.

It was very plain. The other three weren't so plain.

They were approximately footing diameter, round.

Yes, there was a footprint visible. The chief of police explained it over the TV and over the radio.

That's when we stepped on a step, I guess, and walked into the ship.

I was asked, or I asked them to use the telephone.

there, but I didn't. After I seen who he was, he happened to be the assistant county attorney

late for her not to even come for at least two weeks because they had taken me to the
